episode.title: Adapt replayed reasoning fields to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
episode.before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, all otherwise-unrecognized OpenAI-compatible endpoints used the default provider. For Qwen3 model names, that provider copied each assistant history message's non-empty reasoning_content into an additional reasoning field. Because no endpoint-specific adapter was selected for api.fireworks.ai, a multi-turn continuation replaying a thinking turn sent both fields; the strict endpoint rejected messages[N].reasoning with HTTP 400.
episode.after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, exact and subdomain hostnames under api.fireworks.ai select a dedicated provider. After applying the inherited default request transformation, that provider creates a new outbound message array and removes reasoning only when it is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source conversation history, and the existing behavior of non-matching endpoints.
episode.diff: The change adds hostname-bounded provider detection and dispatch, exports a new provider adapter, and overrides the outbound request builder to reverse only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror. It also adds focused routing and field-preservation tests plus an HTTP integration test whose strict local endpoint rejects any assistant reasoning field and confirms that a two-turn thinking-history continuation succeeds with reasoning_content still present on the wire.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a identifies issue #11657 as a failure in which the default Qwen3 transformation adds reasoning beside reasoning_content and the strict endpoint rejects the extra field with HTTP 400; it states that the fix is applied at the outbound boundary without mutating history.

In the parent implementation, DefaultOpenAICompatibleProvider recognizes Qwen3 by model-name substring and maps assistant messages through mirrorReasoningContentToReasoning; the helper returns a copied message with reasoning set to reasoning_content when reasoning_content is a non-empty string and no string reasoning value already exists.
evidence_units.source: git show d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a:packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/provider/default.ts, lines 34-61 and buildRequest around lines 190-211

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, determineProvider checked its known providers through Cerebras and otherwise returned DefaultOpenAICompatibleProvider; it had no routing branch for the affected endpoint.
evidence_units.source: git show d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a:packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/index.ts, determineProvider ending around lines 90-128

evidence_units.claim: The added endpoint detector parses baseUrl, lowercases URL.hostname, accepts only api.fireworks.ai or its dot-delimited subdomains, and returns false for an absent or invalid URL. The implementation explicitly avoids model-name routing because third-party model identifiers are served by the endpoint.

The dedicated provider first delegates to the default request builder, then maps the resulting outbound messages through unmirrorReasoningField. That helper changes only assistant messages whose reasoning is a string equal to reasoning_content, returning a copy without reasoning; role mismatches, unequal values, and non-string values are left unchanged.

determineProvider now constructs the dedicated adapter when its hostname detector matches, before falling back to the default provider. The generation pipeline converts conversation contents into OpenAI messages and invokes provider.buildRequest before request capture and the SDK call, making this the outbound adaptation boundary.

Focused tests assert exact-host and subdomain matching, rejection of a hostile hostname that merely contains the trusted suffix, removal of the mirror while preserving reasoning_content and source history, retention of a distinct explicit reasoning value, and unchanged mirroring for a non-matching endpoint.

An HTTP integration test uses the real generator conversion/provider/wire path and a local strict server that returns the reported 400 shape whenever an assistant message contains reasoning. A follow-up containing a prior thought is accepted, and the captured wire message contains reasoning_content but no reasoning field.
The provider is exported from the provider barrel and public openaiContentGenerator module, and the commit changes four files with 407 inserted lines: routing, exports, the adapter, and its tests.
evidence_units.source: git diff --stat and git diff d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a

evidence_units.claim: Existing default-provider tests establish the behavior that must remain intact: Qwen3 history mirrors reasoning_content without mutating the input, explicit reasoning is not overwritten, and non-Qwen3 models are not mirrored.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-compatible-endpoint-by-canonical-hostname
candidate_atomics.description: Select an endpoint-specific compatibility adapter using parsed hostname boundaries rather than model-family names or substring matching.

semantic_action.intent: Apply a compatibility policy only to requests targeting the endpoint whose wire contract requires it, without misrouting other hosts that serve the same model family.
semantic_action.pre_state: The affected endpoint falls through to a generic compatible-provider implementation, while model identifiers are insufficient to identify the actual endpoint.
semantic_action.post_state: Exact canonical hostname and legitimate subdomains select the specialized adapter; unrelated, hostile-suffix, missing, and invalid URLs do not.
semantic_action.validation: Route exact-host, subdomain, and hostile lookalike URLs through provider selection and assert their resulting request behavior distinguishes matched from fallback endpoints.

candidate_atomics.name: remove-only-derived-incompatible-wire-field
candidate_atomics.description: At the outbound boundary, remove only a field recognizable as a derived mirror while retaining the endpoint-supported source field and distinct explicit values.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent strict-schema request rejection without discarding supported replay data, explicit caller intent, or shared history.
semantic_action.pre_state: An inherited generic transformation has added a reasoning field equal to reasoning_content on an assistant history message, but the selected endpoint rejects reasoning and accepts reasoning_content.
semantic_action.post_state: The outbound copy omits reasoning only when it exactly matches the derived mirror signature; reasoning_content and distinct explicit reasoning values remain, and the source request is unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the mirrored-equality case is removed, unequal explicit values are retained, supported content remains present, source history is not mutated, and fallback providers preserve their prior behavior.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-strict-endpoint-multiturn-continuation
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise the complete history-conversion, provider-adaptation, and HTTP path against a strict contract oracle.

semantic_action.intent: Demonstrate that replaying a prior thinking turn no longer produces a rejected continuation request.
semantic_action.pre_state: A multi-turn request includes an assistant thought that conversion represents as reasoning_content, and a strict endpoint rejects any assistant reasoning property.
semantic_action.post_state: The continuation receives a successful response, with reasoning_content present and reasoning absent in the captured HTTP request.
semantic_action.validation: Use a strict local HTTP server that returns the reported 400 validation payload if reasoning is present, then execute two turns through OpenAIContentGenerator and inspect the second request body.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-generic-compatible-requests-to-a-stricter-endpoint-contract
candidate_workflows.description: Introduce a narrowly routed outbound adapter when a nominally compatible endpoint rejects a generic provider transformation, preserving shared semantics and verifying the complete continuation path.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow thinking-history and tool-call continuations to satisfy the stricter endpoint schema without weakening behavior for other compatible endpoints or deleting supported replay data.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A generic compatible-provider transformation derives an extra message field from preserved history, and the actual endpoint rejects that field during multi-turn continuation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The affected endpoint is safely identified, only the derived incompatible field is removed from an outbound copy, other endpoint behavior is unchanged, and a strict HTTP oracle accepts the continuation wire shape.
unresolved_or_deferred: No independent test-run or CI result is present in the supplied GitHub bundle; the validation oracle is established from committed tests, but execution success was not independently observed in this extraction.

The bundle lacks issue body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks, so the endpoint contract and failure reproduction are grounded in the commit, implementation, and tests rather than discussion metadata.
No cross-repository peers or untouched holdout were provided, so this single workflow must not be promoted as a universal resolution pattern.

unresolved_questions: The issue bundle labels its linked pull-request object as number 11657, while the implementation commit subject references PR #11701 and issue #11657; unavailable GitHub metadata prevents independently resolving that numbering inconsistency.

The checkout working tree is materialized as deletions, so inspection used the pinned commit and parent Git objects. Tests were not executed against the current worktree, and no validation-pass claim is made.

Whether empty or null equal-valued mirrors should be removed is discussed in implementation comments, but the helper's string guard leaves non-string values unchanged; committed tests do not cover empty-string or null cases.
